items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XVI, List of Answers on Terminology 175:1
items.html: It is the nature of every screen to hold back the upper light from passing from its Tabur and downward, and therefore when the upper light meets it, a coupling of striking is made, for it pushes the light backward and raises the reflected light and clothes the direct light, as is known. And sometimes the upper light overcomes the screen and breaks the power of its holding back, and passes through it from there and downward, and this is called breaking and cleaving. And this is at the time of the diminution of the moon, for the nine lower [Sefirot] of the Partzuf of the posterior of the Nukva cleaved the screen and the Parsa beneath Atzilut, and passed through them downward to BYA. (Item 233).
